analysis:
This batch has documentation-only changes. The new file changelog.d/overlapped-weight-verification.md (head lines 1-9) and docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines 621-625) describe a weight-hash optimization. A reader thread stays one 4 MiB chunk ahead of SHA-256 using a second page-aligned F_NOCACHE buffer (OverlappedFileDigest, WeightHasher.uncachedChunkBytes = 4<<20). The docs claim the digests are unchanged and that weights still bypass the file cache.

Relevant threats are T-012, T-027 and A-004 (weight substitution and verification integrity), and T-041, where the verified weightHash binds the SSD prefix cache. No implementation source (WeightHasher, OverlappedFileDigest, PageCache) was supplied, so the docs-only change shows no regression.

Integration and deeper passes should verify the following in the Swift source:
(1) The overlapped reader hashes exactly the bytes read, in order, with no buffer reuse race. The reader must not overwrite a buffer SHA-256 is still consuming.
(2) A short read, EOF or read error fails the hash closed rather than producing a partial digest. The fallback readers must also not mask errors.
(3) The per-file buffers (two 4 MiB buffers per file) are bounded under concurrent hashing. This is a memory and availability concern only.
(4) The fresh pre/post-load hashes for SSD prefix-cache models still detect a file changed during load (time-of-check vs time-of-use).
(5) VerifiedWeightHashStore reuse semantics are unchanged.

Without that source, the integrity of A-004 verification under the new concurrency cannot be confirmed.
